name: Pennsylvania Railroad Exchange Place ferry terminal and train shed (1873)
shape_note: Twelve-track, six-platform terminal on wooden piers built 1873; burnt 4 Aug 1884 after a gas reservoir explosion (Wikipedia timeline). Point: the station coordinates of the article (40.71648 N 74.03238 W), the point of the later terminal, +-40 m. Size, height and shape ESTIMATED (12 tracks and 6 platforms about 55 m across; shed length assumed).

name: Pennsylvania Railroad Exchange Place terminal and train shed (1888-92)
shape_note: Rebuilt 1888-92 and raised 15-20 ft in 1891 (timeline); last PRR passenger train 17 Nov 1961, last buildings demolished 1963 (Wikipedia 'Exchange Place (PRR station)'). Point is the article's station coordinates, +-40 m. Footprint and height ESTIMATED (no plan opened); drawn as one block (shed and head house).

name: Erie Railroad Pavonia Terminal (first)
shape_note: Pavonia terminal opened 1 May 1861; a terminal fire in 1873 (Wikipedia 'Pavonia Terminal'). Point: the article's coordinates, +-40 m. Size, height and the 1873 end ESTIMATED (the fire year is from the article's external links, not read).

name: Erie Railroad Pavonia Terminal (1887)
shape_note: New terminal opened 4 Dec 1887 (NYT, cited in Wikipedia); closed 12 Dec 1958, demolished 1961. Point: the article's coordinates, +-40 m. Footprint and height ESTIMATED (no plan opened); one block for head house, shed and ferry house.

name: Delaware, Lackawanna & Western (Morris & Essex) Hoboken terminal, first and second
shape_note: First terminal 14 Nov 1862, second 15 Jan 1868, burnt June 1873 (Wikipedia 'Hoboken Terminal'). Point: the present terminal's commuter platforms (40.7349 N 74.0277 W, from the article's links), +-40 m. Size ESTIMATED; the two buildings are one row.

name: Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Hoboken terminal (temporary, 1873)
shape_note: Temporary terminal hurriedly built after the June 1873 fire, replaced by the fourth terminal in 1885 (Wikipedia 'Hoboken Terminal'). Point as above. Size ESTIMATED.

name: Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Hoboken terminal (fourth, 1885)
shape_note: Fourth terminal opened 1885; burned in 1905 when the ferry Hopatcong caught fire; replaced by the 1907 terminal that stands (Wikipedia 'Hoboken Terminal'). Point as above, +-40 m. Size and height ESTIMATED.

name: West Shore (New York Central) Weehawken terminal
shape_note: Opened 1884, closed 1959; sixteen passenger tracks, five ferry slips (Wikipedia 'Weehawken Terminal', coordinates 40.771639 N 74.01275 W, +-40 m). Footprint and height ESTIMATED (sixteen tracks about 80 m across, shed length assumed); one block for head house and shed.

name: Lehigh Valley Railroad Black Tom pier, warehouses and rail terminal (destroyed 1916)
shape_note: National Docks Railway of 1883 connected the National Storage Company docks at Black Tom (start year ESTIMATED from it); blown up 30 July 1916, 'over one hundred railroad cars and warehouses' destroyed and a crater of 375 by 175 ft (Wikipedia 'Black Tom explosion', point 40 41 32 N 74 03 20 W, +-40 m). Rebuilt after 1916 (not drawn). Footprint ESTIMATED.
